correctness.rationale: For every prime p>=5, pth-root cyclotomic irreducibility converts a vanishing ambiguity coefficient into a cubic permutation question. The complete conic collision count classifies the latter, while the Weyl diagonalization counts invisible operator directions. Quadratic Gauss magnitudes prove the exact fourth ambiguity moment and Cauchy plus cubic chirp prove sharp comparison. Independent exact integer histogram and phase-difference checks on 13 prime orders, plus direct matrix-rank tests at p=5,7,11, corroborate the all-prime analytic proof. No inference from finite tests to infinite range is made.

originality.rationale: A direct comparison against accessible primary full text and published mathematical-record statements finds no implication covering the combined all-prime quartic ambiguity-zero, lifted rank, and exact fourth-moment theorem. The Weyl diagonalization, permutation-polynomial and quadratic Gauss identities are prior building blocks and are not claimed as original. The isolated p=5 one-coordinate instance can fall under earlier work; novelty is in the all-prime joint classification and moment comparison, subject to residual sequence-design literature risk.
residual_risks: An equivalent zero-set/rank calculation may appear in older polyphase radar sequences or finite-field permutation polynomial literature under different terminology.
The general Weyl diagonalization and exact cubic permutation condition are established; publication priority of the combined quantitative result needs independent specialist review.
